proof_fixes: UNCITED / likely-fabricated stats in the 'Why AI Safety Matters' grid (lines 490-518) violate the honesty rule and expose CSOAI to a credibility/advertising-standards challenge. '£4.5B — Annual cost of AI-driven lending discrimination globally' has no source and is not a defensible figure; '2x', '30%', and '400+' are stated as hard facts with no citation. Fix: either attach a real, linked source under each stat (e.g. a footnote link) or reframe as qualified language — before: 'AI diagnostic tools show significant error rates in diverse populations' / stat '30%'; after: drop the bare number and cite, e.g. 'Studies have found AI diagnostic tools underperform for under-represented groups (source).'

Hyphen used where an em dash is required (grammar). Line 351 button: 'Free AI Risk Check - signed in 2 min' → 'Free AI Risk Check — signed in 2 min'. Line 574: 'browse every regulation - all live' → '…—all live'. Line 575: 'transparency + GPAI go live - run your free signed risk check ->' → '…go live — run your free signed risk check →' (also replace the ASCII '->' arrow with a real '→').

CSS/state bug on the 'Ask the Council' button (line 584): base is `bg-emerald-700` but hover is `hover:bg-emerald-400`, so the button gets LIGHTER on hover — the opposite of every other primary button on the page (which use `hover:bg-emerald-800`). Change to `hover:bg-emerald-800` for consistency.

Duplicate positioning claim + unverifiable superlative. 'The world's first relationship-based AI safety infrastructure' appears in the hero (line 333) and again verbatim in the FAQ answer (line 205). 'World's first' is an unprovable claim for an independent org; use it once, and soften to something defensible, e.g. 'A relationship-based approach to AI safety — partnership, not control.'

Income claims risk breaching UK advertising rules (misleading earnings). 'Earn £45-150/hour' and 'Top analysts working full-time can earn £100,000-300,000+ annually' (lines 229, 923) are presented as expectation, not typical outcome, for a profession the page itself calls 'growing/new'. Add a qualifier — before: 'Top analysts working full-time can earn £100,000-300,000+ annually'; after: 'Rates on the marketplace currently range £45-150/hour; earnings depend on demand, hours, and specialisation.'

Two stacked badges before the H1 (lines 266-289: 'Now Live — open, governed AI-safety infrastructure' + 'Now Live'/'100% Free Training | Only Pay When You Earn') plus the EU countdown push the actual headline far down the fold. Keep one badge above the H1 and move the '100% Free / Only Pay When You Earn' proof point directly beneath the sub-headline as a trust line.

Collapse to ONE primary + ONE secondary above the fold: keep 'Free AI Risk Check — signed in 2 min' as primary and 'Watch the 2-min demo' as secondary; demote 'Start free', 'Try Sov Space', and the globe/network/watchdog pills into the 'Five doors into the Sovereign OS' strip that already exists lower down.

# CSOAI Landing-Page Enhancement Plan
_8-page audit synthesis · lead recommendation · 2026-07-08_

Files audited: `client/src/pages/NewHome-v2.tsx`, `Compare.tsx`, `SECDisclosure.tsx`, `SectorAct.tsx` (+ 4 sibling sector/persona pages sharing the same components). The single recurring theme across all pages: **the word "signed" is asserted but never shown, uncited numbers create honesty-register/ASA exposure, and hero CTAs are diffuse.** The moat (Ed25519-signed, offline-verifiable, cross-framework consensus) is buried in text everywhere and dramatized nowhere.

---

## A. Top 10 highest-impact copy/proof fixes (page + exact change)

1. **Homepage — kill the uncited stat grid (NewHome-v2.tsx, lines 490–518).** Remove or source-link `£4.5B`, `2x`, `30%`, `400+`. These are stated as hard facts with zero citation = honesty-register violation + UK ASA/advertising risk. Fix: attach a linked footnote source under each, or reframe qualitatively ("Studies have found AI diagnostic tools underperform for under-represented groups [source]"). **Highest legal-exposure item on the whole site.**

2. **Homepage — de-risk the income claims (lines 229, 923).** "Earn £45–150/hour" and "£100,000–300,000+ annually" presented as expectation breach UK misleading-earnings rules. Change to: "Rates on the marketplace currently range £45–150/hour; earnings depend on demand, hours, and specialisation."
